title: Add TP runtime instrumentation (per-rank progress, collective latency histograms, structured logs)
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Goal
Add the missing runtime observability needed to quickly distinguish:
- comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation
- a single rank lagging vs full TP group deadlock
- cancellation-induced barrier issues vs NCCL async error propagation

This ticket covers instrumentation only (metrics + structured logs + lightweight trace/span annotations). It should enable:
1) fast triage during an incident (oncall can answer “what is stuck and where?” in <5 min)
2) watchdog/quarantine correctness verification (avoid false positives)
3) regression detection in perf-canary/CI stress suites

Scope
A) Metrics
1) Per-rank forward progress counters
- Counter or gauge that advances when a rank completes meaningful work, not just loops.
- Prefer per TP-group + rank label only when group cardinality is bounded; otherwise aggregate at host/pool level with sampling.

Proposed (final naming subject to Observability Pack conventions):
- runtime_tp_rank_progress_tokens_total{deployment_mode, pool, model, tp_size, rank}
  - Increment by generated tokens processed on that rank (or by “steps” if tokens are hard in the kernel path).
- runtime_tp_rank_last_progress_timestamp_seconds{...}
  - Gauge updated on each progress event (useful for “time since last progress”).
- runtime_tp_group_inflight_requests{deployment_mode, pool, model, tp_size, group_id_hash}
  - Optional; use hashed group id to cap cardinality.

2) Collective latency histograms
We need p50/p95/p99 of common collectives and an easy way to spot tail blowups preceding hangs.
- runtime_tp_collective_latency_seconds_bucket{collective, model, tp_size, gpu_type, driver, nccl_version}
  - collective in {all_reduce, all_gather, reduce_scatter, broadcast}
  - MUST avoid high-cardinality labels (no request_id, no full group UUID).
- runtime_tp_collective_timeout_total{collective, model, tp_size}
  - increment when collective crosses the configured timeout threshold (even if it later completes).

3) Scheduler starvation vs comm stall signal
- runtime_tp_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds_bucket{queue, model, tp_size}
- runtime_tp_group_barrier_wait_seconds_bucket{barrier_type, model, tp_size}

B) Structured logs (for hang signatures)
Add structured log events that can be correlated by tp_group_id + request_id (request_id may be sampled).
Required log events:
- tp_collective_stall_detected
  - fields: tp_group_id, rank, collective, elapsed_ms, seq_len, batch_size, model, gpu, stream_id (if available), nccl_async_error (bool), nccl_error_code (optional), watchdog_context (optional)
- tp_scheduler_starvation_detected
  - fields: tp_group_id, rank (optional), elapsed_ms, runnable_count, blocked_reason (barrier|cancel|capacity), model
- tp_request_canceled_during_barrier
  - fields: tp_group_id, rank, barrier_type, request_id, phase, cancel_reason (client_disconnect|deadline|server_abort)

Logging requirements:
- default INFO only for summarized stall detection events; DEBUG for per-iteration spam
- sampling: 1/N for repeated stall events per tp_group_id to avoid log storms
- ensure logs are emitted on a non-critical path (don’t introduce heavy synchronization)

C) Trace/span annotations
If tracing is enabled, annotate spans around collectives/barriers with:
- collective type
- elapsed
- rank
- tp_size
This should be optional and off by default in Hosted hot paths.

Acceptance criteria
- New metrics are emitted in staging under TP workloads and appear on the TP Collectives/Scheduler Health dashboard.
- No >1% throughput regression in perf microbenchmarks attributable to instrumentation (measure with/without flags).
- Oncall can, using only dashboard + logs, determine which of these is occurring:
  (1) comm stall (collective latency tails)
  (2) kernel stall (progress counters stop, collectives not active)
  (3) scheduler starvation (queue wait spikes, barrier wait)
- Instrumentation is gated behind config flags with safe defaults for Hosted and Dedicated.

Implementation notes / guardrails
- Cardinality: do NOT label metrics with request_id, full tp_group UUID, pod name, etc. Use stable low-card labels (model family, tp_size, collective). If group-level is needed, use a short hash and cap number of active series.
- Timestamps: prefer monotonic clock for elapsed timers; use wall clock only for log fields.
- Sampling strategy should be deterministic per tp_group_id to keep repeated events consistent.

Links
- Umbrella: ENG-2401
- Related issues: ENG-2407 (watchdog), ENG-2406 (async error checks)
- Dashboard spec: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tp-collectives-and-scheduler-health-dashboard.json
- Debugging playbook: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/debugging-tp-hangs-playbook.json

Planned PR(s)
- Primary: PR #18470 (structured logs + trace annotations)
- Follow-ups (if needed): PR for metric naming tweaks per Observability Pack review

Rollout
- Stage in perf-canary first; validate no log storms under overload.
- Enable metrics by default; keep detailed per-rank logging behind flag in Hosted.
- Dedicated: enable higher-fidelity metrics/logging for customers in active escalations (via feature flag).
comments: 2025-02-18 (Noah Patel): Prioritize this; we’re blind during incidents and can’t quickly answer comm vs kernel vs scheduler. Please coordinate metric names/labels with Allison (Observability standards) to avoid cardinality traps.

2025-02-19 (Allison Grant): Please avoid tp_group_id as a direct label in Prometheus. If you need group correlation, put it in logs/traces; metrics should aggregate. For per-rank metrics, keep rank + tp_size only if series count stays bounded per host/pool.

2025-02-20 (Omar El-Sayed): Drafted metric set + log schema. Biggest question: token-based progress vs “step” progress. Token count is easiest in decoder loop; kernel path doesn’t always see token boundaries. Proposal: use progress_steps_total in kernel + map to tokens in higher layer where possible.

2025-02-21 (Sofia Ivanova): For starvation detection, we need to separate “blocked on barrier” from “blocked on capacity”. Please add barrier_wait histogram and include barrier_type (pre_fill|decode|flush|teardown) in logs.

2025-02-22 (Sean Gallagher): Oncall needs a single log line when we cross “suspected stall” threshold with enough context to decide mitigation (shift traffic vs quarantine vs restart). Sampling is fine but first event per group should always be logged.

2025-02-24 (Omar El-Sayed): Implemented tp_collective_stall_detected event with first-event-always + rate-limited repeats. Added trace annotations around collectives guarded by runtime.enable_tp_collective_spans=false default.
2025-02-25 (Sergio Costa): For the dashboard panels, I need final metric names and label set by EOW. Please confirm histogram buckets and whether we can break down by collective type + tp_size.

2025-02-26 (Omar El-Sayed): Updated names to runtime_tp_collective_latency_seconds + runtime_tp_scheduler_queue_wait_seconds. Buckets: [1ms, 2ms, 5ms, 10ms, 25ms, 50ms, 100ms, 250ms, 500ms, 1s, 2s, 5s, 10s].
2025-02-28 (Julian Moore): Added per-rank last_progress_timestamp gauge update in decode loop. Verified negligible overhead with sampling 1/8 for high-QPS pools; Dedicated can set to 1/1 if needed.

2025-03-03 (Omar El-Sayed): PR #18470 up for review. Includes: structured logs for collective stalls + scheduler starvation, span annotations, and a small helper to compute deterministic sampling by tp_group_id hash.
2025-03-04 (Grace Kim): Reviewed PR. One nit: ensure we don’t call expensive string formatting on hot path when log level is disabled. Please guard JSON construction behind logger.is_enabled(INFO).
2025-03-05 (Omar El-Sayed): Fixed hot-path formatting + added unit test for sampling (first event always logged, repeats rate-limited).

2025-03-06 (Omar El-Sayed): Merged PR #18470. Verified metrics in staging and dashboard panels show expected distributions under synthetic TP load. Marking Done; any metric naming tweaks will be follow-up in Observability Pack PR.
